_about: Modules: what a machine wears inside, beside its die (bible section 10, the modules row). A chassis carries module_slots of them (two as a rule, three on the Clydesdale; a number of the chassis, never bought). A module is read like a passive: any number of stat lines (stats: the engine's stat names, hull, shield, heat, armour, move, recharge, cooling, added through Effects) beside at most one text (text: a description shown to the player and its effects, checked like a passive's; a text the engine cannot run carries "status": "planned"). Every module has a tier, 1 to 3, so the first battle offers plain ones; the capital's maker has no tier one. The archetypes (plate, kit, overload, prototype) are a design guide, never stored or checked. Shown: name, codex, flavour, the text's description; internal text under design.

design.fantasy: Bolt-on armour that comes off in sheets so the hull does not.
design.niche: A plate: plain stats, the starting module.
design.notes: A component until 9 October (Minerva's shield 20); Ryan moved the platings to modules the same day, since a hardpoint is a mount and armour is not mounted. It took the place of Claude's Slab Armour, which did the same job.

text.description: Its Direct blows aimed at the front rank deal 1 more.

design.fantasy: A reinforced prow and a driver who stopped asking.
design.niche: A reach read (Ryan, 22 October): +1 on Direct blows aimed at the front rank, the Artillery Rangefinder its mirror at the back for Indirect blows. Without a rule it measured the best module on every machine (the bible's catalogue row); its armour line went with the rule, and its stat line comes from the pricing run after the landing.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; its old rule gave every weapon melee reach, gone with Close (10 October). Ryan's call of 22 October, on Claude's second proposal: the mirrors; built 22 October (target_rank with a reach). Numbers are placeholders.

text.description: Taking hull damage stands up 2 shield.

design.fantasy: A lining that catches what comes off the inside of the armour, and throws it back out as a wall.
design.niche: A prototype: a slower, hotter machine that never takes two bare-hull blows running.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders. Needed the on_hull_damage shield fix (built 9 October).

text.description: Each time its heat climbs, it stands up 1 shield.

design.fantasy: Bleed air off the hot skin and blow it across the hull as a cushion.
design.niche: A kit: a small stat and a small rule; a hot machine is a shielded one.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: Everything leaves the barrel faster. Including the barrel, eventually.
design.niche: The ceiling to the Tactical Databank's floor: a rolled weapon's highest roll raised a little.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders. 10 October (Ryan): no crits, so it raises the top of the range instead (it was triple-damage crits); never tuned to parity with the Databank, since a module carries stats too. Then (Ryan): mirror images with the Databank, 5 each with no stats (its -20 shield was left over from the crit module), until the runner's module rows measure them.

text.description: Its weapons run twice as hot.

design.fantasy: Afterburners on the walk to the fight, and the fight paid for in heat.
design.niche: An overload: speed and shield for double heat; a perk on a machine that wants heat (the Goshawk).
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: A little armour is better than the amount you had.
design.niche: A plate: plain stats, the starting module.
design.notes: A component until 9 October (W&S's shield 10); moved to modules with the other platings the same day (Ryan).

design.fantasy: Radiator grilles off a field kitchen, bolted wherever they fit.
design.niche: A plate for heat: a hotter, cooler machine.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders.

text.description: Its rolled weapons' lowest roll is 1 higher.

design.fantasy: Every firing solution the regiment ever logged, in a box that hums.
design.niche: The floor to the Muzzle Velocity Booster's ceiling: a rolled weapon's lowest roll raised a little, with a little hull stapled on so it is worth a slot.
design.notes: The Dingo's passive until 8 October, then the game's first module with its name kept (Ryan), with an ally in the fight. The ally condition was there so the Dingo's stealth could not carry it alone; stealth is gone, and Ryan said it may not be needed (9 October), so it is dropped for the runner to judge (Claude's lean; a raised minimum is the lighter fallback). 10 October (Ryan): a flat increase in place of rolling the maximum, more interesting and far less abusable; no stat line, and never tuned to parity with the Booster (a module carries stats too; the runner's module rows are the guard against a must-pick). Later on 10 October (Ryan, as on 9 October: increase the minimum instead of maxing it): the floor raised by a small amount, stats stapled on if that is too weak; the +5 on every blow was a flat damage increase, good everywhere and so bad design. Hull +20 is Claude's placeholder until the runner's module rows read it. Then (Ryan): no reason, and no data, for a stat on one and a cost on the other, so the Databank and the Booster are mirror images, the floor and the ceiling 5 each with no stats, until the runner's module rows measure them.

text.description: Its Indirect blows aimed at the back rank deal 1 more.

design.fantasy: A man with a theodolite who has never once been wrong about where a shell lands.
design.niche: The Ram Frame's mirror (Ryan, 22 October): a reach read, +1 on Indirect blows aimed at the back rank, where the Frame reads Direct blows at the front; its stat line comes from the pricing run after the landing.
design.notes: Ryan, 9 October: the Rangefinder as named fits a splash-damage eliminator (Claude's earlier versions rolled indirect weapons high, too near the Databank). 22 October (the stock pass's engine): danger close retired, so its rule went with it. Ryan's call the same day, on Claude's second proposal: the Ram Frame and the Rangefinder are mirrors, each a reach read; built 22 October (target_rank with a reach). The number is a placeholder.

text.description: An ally it shields is Armoured 1 for the round.

design.fantasy: The field it lends comes back mirrored, and the mirror holds.
design.niche: A kit for the support frame: a shield spent on an ally is armour too.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders. Needed the on_shield_granted fix, the status on the ally (built 9 October). 18 October: Armoured 3 a shield (a stack of Braced, +5, before; a stack is an armour point now), a placeholder.

text.description: Its blows deal 1 more to a foe carrying any status.

design.fantasy: A matrix of how much each thing in front of it wants to fall apart.
design.niche: A kit: a status machine's payoff.
design.notes: Claude's Tactical Plotting Board for W&S, 9 October; Ryan the same day: the effect reads as Aphelion's, so it moved and took an Aphelion name (Claude's working name, for Ryan to move). +5, not +10: a flat modifier on the player's blows, brought down with them by the damage scale (bible section 11).

text.description: Every blow on it lands 2 harder.

design.fantasy: A shell of something with negative mass. Hits do not quite agree with it.
design.niche: An overload: a huge shield that every small hit chews into.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders.

design.fantasy: Armour inscribed with the Arsenal's tolerances. It holds because it was told to.
design.niche: A plate, at tier two: the Arsenal fields no tier one.
design.notes: A component until 9 October (the Arsenal's shield 20); moved to modules with the other platings the same day (Ryan). It took the place of Claude's Consecrated Plate.

text.description: Taking hull damage Overcharges it, a stack a blow.

design.fantasy: It keeps a record of every wound, and it reads the list aloud.
design.niche: A kit: a machine that hits harder the more it is hit.
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders. 18 October: a stack a blow at a point a stack, halving each round, so a machine struck so often a round settles near twice that; the bench, a stack for every 5 hull lost.

text.description: Every component it spends costs 3 hull.

design.fantasy: The machine takes its due before it does anything you ask.
design.niche: An overload: a great deal of hull and shield with a price on every action; a perk where the hull is already being spent (the Nemesis).
design.notes: Claude's proposal of 9 October, in Ryan's pick of the whole catalogue the same day; numbers are placeholders.

text.description: Rerolling only its own die is free once a round.

design.fantasy: Small hinged tabs on every control surface, trimmed in flight: the airframe settles onto whatever it was aiming for.
design.niche: The Kestrel line's reroll module: another look at its own die, a free reroll a round, paid in heat maximum so no module is the universal pick.
design.notes: Taken in the Kestrel line review (21 October, docs/briefs/kestrel_line.md); landed with the stock pass (22 October), the stat line its price. Numbers are placeholders.
